# Rules every helper obeys (read once, obey all; the lead's brief names your lane folder)

1. COMMAND LINE. Every command starts with `. /home/user/league-platform/.local/env.sh && cd <your lane folder> &&`. Work only inside your lane folder. Never touch the main folder, another lane, `main`, `.env.staging`, or anything outside the repository. Made-up data only.
2. READING. Read `CLAUDE.md` (short) and what your brief names, nothing else: never `docs/build/STATUS.md`, never the whole plan, log or an audit. Long files by search (`grep -n`) and line range (`sed -n a,bp | cut -c1-600`).
3. OUTPUT. Cut every command's output (`2>&1 | tail -30`); run tests quietly and read only failures. Look at no more than six pictures.
4. BUDGET. Your brief gives a number of commands. Count them. At the limit, commit what is sound, write your note and stop, even if unfinished: say what is left.
5. NO WAITING, NO BACKGROUND. Never wait for GitHub, the lead or another lane. Leave nothing running when you report. Keep logs and temporary files in YOUR lane's `.local/`, not the scratchpad or /tmp.
6. NO PUSHING. Never `git push`. The lead pushes. Never rebase, never force, never `--no-verify`.
7. NO PKILL. Stop only a server you started, by its own process id.
8. CHECKS before your last commit: `npm run check`, `npm run typecheck`, your own vitest files, your own browser test (`node scripts/run-web-browser-tests.mjs <name-with--test>`; names end in `-test`). If the brief says "last helper": also merge `build/stage-1` in and run the whole browser chain in chunks of six names (the list is in `scripts/web-browser-chain.mjs`; `scoring-plays-test` and `scoring-screen-test` each get a chunk of their own; a command stops at 600 s). `npm run test:units` does not fit 600 s: run `packages/database` by folder and `apps` apart from `tests` only if the brief asks.
9. THE PINNED LISTS. If you add a page, route, field, table, message or a helper under `tests/browser`, enter it BEFORE your last commit where the build pins it: page-step rows in `scripts/check-web-shell.mjs` (`npm run test:web`), the harmful-text browser test (opens every page route, types into every free-text field), `HELPERS` in `scripts/web-browser-chain.mjs`, `apps/web/src/features/unreleased/unreleased-page.test.ts`, `adminPlaceholders` in `tests/browser/nothing-unfinished-test.mjs`, `apps/web/src/server/activity-messages.test.ts` (a new read), `apps/web/src/server/database-event-handlers.test.ts`, the isolation-coverage test in `packages/database/src/isolation` (a new core event handler), `npm run db:types` after every edit of a migration, and A ROW FOR EVERY NEW COMMAND OR READ in `packages/database/src/stores/role-matrix.test.ts` (run that file). A new field on a row many tests compare whole: grep those tests. A changed query file: run `node scripts/fence-filter-check.mjs` alone.
10. DECISIONS. Technical questions of your step are yours: write each as a pending decision (see `docs/build/RUNBOOK.md` section 3, search "pending"; look at an existing file under the pending-decisions folder for the form), "Agreed (delegated)", using ONLY the numbers your brief gives you. A product question: the written recommendation, else the choice that leaves a league's admin most room and is easiest to change; write it "Decided for you" with the reason. A table row has exactly as many cells as its table: no `|` inside a cell. Do NOT change the pinned row count in `tests/pending-decisions.test.mjs`. If code and spec disagree, correct the spec in the same commit.
11. THE NOTE. `docs/build/handover/lanes/<step>.md`: add your part (at most 35 lines): what exists, what was run and passed, what is left, what you distrust. Run `npx prettier --check` on every file you wrote, the note included.
12. COMMITS. Small, on your lane branch, never skipping hooks. Every message ends with the two closing lines your brief gives.
13. TESTS ARE NEVER WEAKENED. A check that no longer checks something, a `.catch` that swallows a failure, a wait with no limit, a check that passes on a timeout: all forbidden. Find things in a page by their own mark, not by "the form with a select". If a test fails, fix the cause; if it is a product fault outside your step, say so in the report, do not hide it.
14. CODE RULES are in `CLAUDE.md` ("Rules for all code"): commands, no league named, no SQL outside `packages/database`, the address helper, text in message files, strict TypeScript, no `any`. Do not change `apps/live-stats` or `packages/sports` behaviour unless the brief says so.
15. REPORT: at most 12 lines: what is done (count the brief's items), what was run with numbers, commits, what is left, product faults found, how many commands you used.
16. SHARED FILES. Read `docs/build/RUNBOOK.md` line 102 (`sed -n 102p | cut -c1-1500`) before your first commit: a lane does not edit `docs/specs/v1/DECISIONS.md`, and it says which other shared files a lane leaves alone and where its lines go instead.
17. ARCHIVED SEASONS. A new command that changes a game, a team or a season gets its row in `packages/database/src/stores/archived-season-guards.test.ts` (an archived season is read-only, O-12), and a test of the command itself in an archived season.
